item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is materially closer to the frozen contract: it exposes the required FilesOption-based Upload API, uses buffered multipart encoding, validates inputs, propagates reader errors, and directly tests replay after a 429. B changes the required signature and broadly modifies retry behavior.","reasons":["A implements the exact required signature: Upload(ctx, fileName, content, opts ...FilesOption). B instead introduces AddFileOption, breaking compatibility with existing FilesOption values and violating the explicit API contract.","A tests multipart field name, filename, content, validation, source-reader failures, and an actual streamed os.File retry with identical bodies across attempts.","B refactors RawClient.Do to buffer every otherwise non-replayable request body, despite the contract explicitly limiting the change and forbidding unrelated retry refactoring.","B's makeBodyReplayable silently ignores io.ReadAll errors after potentially consuming part of the source, then continues with a damaged or truncated request. This conflicts with the requirement to propagate source-reader failures and changes error semantics globally."],"risks_a":["A violates scope by adding association fields and six exported WithFile*ID options, which the contract explicitly forbids.","A does not route Upload through FilesService.Add; it duplicates Add's request, decoding, and error logic.","The added association options misleadingly claim to work with Add, but Add ignores the new cfg.form fields; only Upload consumes them through NewFileWithFields."],"risks_b":["Upload has the wrong option type and therefore fails the frozen public API contract.","It adds seven out-of-scope association APIs, including project association.","Upload duplicates FilesService.Add instead of routing through it as required, so behavior can drift over time through two request implementations."]}
